newsitem.title: KENYA: More than 130 killed, 1,500 wounded in Mogadishu.
newsitem.headline: More than 130 killed, 1,500 wounded in Mogadishu.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said on Friday 1,500 people were admitted to Mogadishu hospitals with wounds from fierce fighting in the Somali capital in the past week.

ICRC Somalia spokesman Claude Voillat said 132 people had died of their wounds in Mogadishu hospitals but the overall death toll from the fighting was probably much higher because people killed on the spot were not taken to hospitals.
"From December 13 until Thursday we had around 1,500 war wounded admitted. We have 132 deaths but these are only the ones who died in hospitals," said Voillat, after an ICRC survey of the cpaital.
Voillat told Reuters the bulk of the casualties were at Medina hospital, overflowing with wounded, and the ICRC and Somali Red Crescent were trying to send medical supplies there.

The seaside Medina district is virtually besieged by forces loyal to south Mogadishu faction leader Hussein Aideed. But some wounded are smuggled over frontlines to hospitals elsewhere in the capital.
The ICRC flew eight tonnes of medical supplies to Mogadishu on Monday. Voillat said daily ICRC flights were taking small amounts of supplies to the city from Nairobi including one tonne on Thursday.
Some shelling from north Mogadishu to southern Mogadishu was reported overnight after a lull on Thursday allowed dozens of families to flee their homes for safer parts of the city.

Shooting and shelling since last Friday has pitted Aideed's militiamen against forces of his rivals -- Hassan Ali Osman Atto in south Mogadishu, Ali Mahdi Mohamed in north Mogadishu and Moslem fundamentalist leader Musa Sudi Yalahow in Medina.

Hussein Aideed, a 34-year-old former U.S. marine, succeeded his father Mohamed Farah Aideed on his death in August. He was elected president of Somalia by his supporters but both he and his government are rejected by most other faction leaders.
